mainTopic: Designated doves found out of place, then the משנה's disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל about a pestle, a hide, and preserving fats on יום טוב.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of designated (זימון) young doves. The גמרא tries to prove רבי חנינא's rule that רוב beats קרוב from the משנה. אביי rejects the proof by placing the case on a shared ledge (דף), and רבא rejects it by placing it in two stacked nests. It then explains why birds found alone are permitted: hopping birds travel at most 50 אמות, and only while they can still see their nest. A new משנה follows, with disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל about using a pestle (עלי) to cut meat on יום טוב and about placing a raw hide where people will tread on it. אביי limits the pestle dispute: a bone-breaking anvil is permitted by everyone, even a new one, because once an animal is slaughtered its bones will surely be broken. On the hide, both sides allow salting meat for roasting on it, but not heavy, pot-style salting. A ברייתא then brings a dispute about airing out the forbidden fats (חלבים), and רב מתנה's ruling on it is reported in two opposite versions. The amud ends by asking how the fats differ from the hide case, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the previous explanation: the knot wears out
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of an earlier answer. A tie holding two items together can wear loose, so one item may be taken without the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: …because their knot wears out.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the final words of an explanation from the previous page. It explains that the knot tying two items together can wear out and come undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the knot can rot and loosen, we cannot assume the two items stayed together. It is possible that someone took only one of them. This finishes the earlier discussion before the גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה.

phrases.english: for their knot wears out (and comes undone).
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from the previous page. It explains why one of the two tied items could have been taken on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמִתְעַכַּל קִטְרַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzMaskana: We cannot assume the tied items stayed together, because the knot may have come undone.

steps.title: The משנה: designated inside the nest, found in front of it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling. Doves designated inside the nest but found in front of the nest are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he designated doves inside the nest and found doves in front of the nest, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to begin a new discussion. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will try to use this line as a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יום טוב a person must designate (זימון) the young doves he plans to use. Here he designated birds inside the nest but later found birds just outside it. The משנה forbids them because they may not be the same birds he designated.
steps.confusionAlert: The birds are forbidden only because we are not sure they are the designated ones. If we knew they were the same birds, they would be permitted.

phrases.aramaic: בְּתוֹךְ הַקֵּן וּמָצָא לִפְנֵי הַקֵּן — אֲסוּרִין.
phrases.english: (If he designated) inside the nest and found (birds) in front of the nest — they are forbidden.
phrases.notes: A quotation from the משנה (דיבור המתחיל).

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּתוֹךְ הַקֵּן וּמָצָא לִפְנֵי הַקֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a new line from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds designated inside the nest but found in front of it are forbidden.

steps.title: Does this support רבי חנינא's rule of following the majority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה supports רבי חנינא, who says that when רוב and קרוב conflict, we follow the רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports רבי חנינא? For רבי חנינא said: when there is a majority and something nearby, follow the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the משנה's ruling proves רבי חנינא's rule. In that rule, 'majority' beats 'nearness.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The birds in front of the nest are close to the designated nest (קרוב), which suggests they are the designated birds. But most doves in the world come from elsewhere (רוב). Since the משנה forbids them, it seems to follow the רוב over the קרוב, just as רבי חנינא rules.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say this supports him

steps.whyThisMatters: רוב versus קרוב is a basic question about how הלכה decides cases of doubt. A proof from a משנה would carry real weight.

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports Rabbi Chanina?
For Rabbi Chanina said:
(When there is) a majority and (something) near — follow the majority!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה just quoted as a proof for an אמורא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's rule that רוב beats קרוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה forbids birds found right in front of the designated nest.

steps.title: אביי: the case involves a ledge in front of the nests
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The משנה is talking about birds found on a ledge where birds from all nests gather.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: (The case is) on a ledge.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof. He explains that the משנה's case is different from a true רוב-versus-קרוב case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the birds were found on a ledge (דף) that all the birds use, then being 'in front of the nest' does not make them closer to this nest than to any other. So there is no real קרוב here, only a doubt. The משנה therefore tells us nothing about which factor wins.

keyTerms.meaning: a board or ledge attached in front of the nests

phrases.english: Abaye said: (We are dealing) with a ledge.
phrases.notes: אביי means the birds were found on a shared ledge where birds from every nest gather.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּדַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 3 by redefining the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself. It does not reject רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a real 'near' factor, but on a shared ledge there is none.

steps.title: רבא: two nests, one above the other — the simple case
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof differently. The case involves two stacked nests. He first gives the obvious case: designated in the lower nest, found birds only in the lower nest, and they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We are dealing with two nests, one above the other. It does not need to be said that if he designated in the lower one and not the upper, and found birds in the lower and none in the upper, they are forbidden. For we say: those went off into the world, and these slid down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second way to reject the proof. He sets the case in two nests stacked on top of each other and begins with the easier example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two nests right next to each other, both are equally 'near,' so this is not a רוב-versus-קרוב question. If he designated the lower nest and the upper one is now empty, we fear the designated birds flew away and the birds from above slid down into the lower nest. That is why they are forbidden. Sliding down is easy, so this case is obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: it does not need to be said
the lower nest / the upper nest

steps.confusionAlert: 'ולא מבעיא' introduces the easier case first. רבא's real new point comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁנֵי קִנִּין זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ עָסְקִינַן.
phrases.english: We are dealing with two nests, one above the other.
And it need not be said (that if) he designated in the lower one
and did not designate in the upper one,
and he found (birds) in the lower and did not find (any) in the upper
— that they are forbidden, for we say:
those (designated ones) went off into the world,
and these (from above) dragged themselves along and came down.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בִּשְׁנֵי קִנִּין זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different rejection of the proof from step 3, parallel to אביי's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof. The משנה's case involves two equally near nests, not רוב against קרוב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed one nest was 'near,' but with stacked nests both are equally near.

steps.title: רבא's real point: even birds in the upper nest are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא's new point: even if he designated the upper nest and found birds only there, they are forbidden. The birds from below may have climbed up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, even if he designated in the upper one and not the lower, and came and found birds in the upper and none in the lower, these too are forbidden. For we say: those went off into the world, and these clutched and climbed up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his real new point with 'אלא אפילו' ('rather, even'). The harder case is also forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think young birds cannot climb up, so birds found in the upper nest must be the designated ones. רבא says we still worry that the lower birds clung and climbed up while the designated birds flew away. So both directions create doubt, and the birds are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, even (introduces the bigger new point)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא does not accept the proof for רבי חנינא. אביי sets the case on a shared ledge. רבא sets it in two stacked nests, where birds can slide down and can even climb up, so in either direction we cannot be sure they are the designated birds.

phrases.english: Rather, even if he designated in the upper one
and did not designate in the lower one,
and he came and found (birds) in the upper one
and did not find (any) in the lower one —
these too are forbidden, for we say:
those (designated ones) went off into the world,
and these (from below) clutched and climbed up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ זִמֵּן בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה וְלֹא זִמֵּן בַּתַּחְתּוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the easier case in step 5 to give רבא's real new point.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Completes רבא's rejection of the proof for רבי חנינא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The doubt comes from the birds possibly moving between equally near nests, not from רוב against קרוב.

steps.title: The משנה's second ruling: if only these birds are there, they are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה. If the only birds present are these, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there are no birds there except them, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה so it can explain it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, birds found in front of the nest were forbidden, because they might have come from somewhere else. Here no other birds are around, so we assume these are the birds he set aside. The גמרא now wants to know exactly what case this is.

keyTerms.meaning: there are only these birds there

phrases.english: And if there are none there except them —
these are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first clause of the משנה to its second clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If no other birds are present, the found birds are permitted.

steps.title: It cannot be about birds that fly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means. It cannot mean birds that fly, because the original birds may have flown away and these may be new birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it is about birds that can fly, you could argue that the original ones flew off into the world and these are different birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kind of baby birds the משנה is talking about. It rules out birds that can already fly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird that flies can travel any distance. So even if only these birds are here, they could be strangers from far away. That is no reason to permit them, so the משנה must mean a different kind of bird.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? (what exactly are the circumstances)
young birds that can already fly
if you say (opens a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say it is about birds that can fly,
one could say:
those (the designated ones) went off into the world,
and these are other birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא בִּמְפוֹרָחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case behind the ruling just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permit in the משנה's second clause
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Birds that fly could have come from anywhere, so finding only these birds proves nothing.

steps.title: Hopping birds: if a nest is near, they could have hopped over
steps.stepSummary: So the משנה must mean birds that only hop. But if another nest is within 50 אמות, these birds could have hopped over from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about birds that hop. But if there is another nest within fifty אמות, they could have hopped over from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the case of hopping birds and finds the first side of a problem. If a nest is close by, the birds could have come from there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hopping birds cannot go far, but they can travel some distance. If another nest is close enough, these may be its birds, and they should be forbidden. That does not match the משנה's ruling of מותר.

keyTerms.meaning: young birds that hop but cannot yet fly

phrases.english: Rather, it is about birds that hop.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּאִיכָּא קֵן בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה —
phrases.english: If there is a nest within fifty cubits —
they could have hopped over from it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּמִדַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from flying birds to hopping birds, then challenges one version of that case.
steps.kashyaTarget: Hopping birds with a nest nearby
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Birds from a nearby nest could have hopped over, so they should be forbidden.

steps.title: If no nest is near, the ruling is too obvious
steps.stepSummary: If no nest is within 50 אמות, it is obvious the birds are permitted, because a hopping bird never goes past 50 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there is no nest within fifty אמות, it is obvious that they are permitted. As מר עוקבא בר חמא said: any creature that hops does not hop more than fifty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the problem. With no nearby nest, the משנה would be teaching something too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר עוקבא בר חמא teaches that a hopping bird never travels past 50 אמות. If no other nest is that close, these birds could not have come from anywhere else. A משנה does not bother teaching something that simple, so neither version of the hopping case seems to work.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious (so why teach it?)
fifty cubits, the most a hopping bird travels
the אמורא who teaches the 50-אמה rule

steps.confusionAlert: There are two sides here, and both cause a problem. A nest that is near makes the birds forbidden. No nest near makes the ruling obvious. The answer in the next step is a case in between.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי דְּלֵיכָּא קֵן בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה —
phrases.english: and if there is no nest within fifty cubits —
it is obvious that they are permitted,
as מר עוקבא בר חמא said:
any creature that hops —
does not hop more than fifty cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי דְּלֵיכָּא קֵן בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה פְּשִׁיטָא דְּמוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the problem with hopping birds.
steps.kashyaTarget: Hopping birds with no nest nearby
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling would be obvious, so the משנה would have no reason to teach it.

steps.title: The nearby nest is around a corner
steps.stepSummary: The answer: there is a nest within 50 אמות, but it is around a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, there is a nest within fifty אמות, but it is a case where that nest stands around a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by picking a case in between the two sides. The other nest is close, but it is around a corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nest is close enough to cause a doubt, so the ruling is not obvious. But because it is around a corner, the birds could not have hopped from it. The next step explains why a corner makes the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: really (we keep the earlier case and explain it better)

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיכָּא קֵן בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה,
phrases.english: Really, there is a nest within fifty cubits,
and it is a case where it stands around a corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיכָּא קֵן בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided problem from steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nest is either near, so the birds are forbidden, or far, so the ruling is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nest is near but around a corner, so the birds are permitted and the ruling is not obvious.

steps.title: A hopping bird only keeps going while it can see its nest
steps.stepSummary: The new lesson is that a hopping bird keeps hopping only while it can turn and still see its nest. Once its nest is out of sight, it stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said they hopped over. So the משנה teaches us: wherever a bird hops and can turn back and see its nest, it keeps hopping. If it cannot see its nest, it does not hop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what new idea the משנה teaches with this case. It is about how hopping birds behave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought the birds from the nearby nest hopped over, since it is within 50 אמות. But a hopping bird does not go anywhere it cannot see its home. A nest around a corner is out of sight, so these birds could not have come from it, and they are permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: A hopping bird goes at most 50 אמות, and only as long as it can still see its own nest. A nest around a corner does not cause a doubt, so birds found alone are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a second limit on how far a hopping bird travels. Besides the 50 אמות, the bird must be able to see its nest.

phrases.english: You might have said:
they hopped over from there,
so it teaches us
wherever it hops
and can turn back and see its nest — it keeps hopping,
and if not — it does not hop.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא אִדַּדּוֹיֵי אִדַּדּוֹ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the corner case answers the problem.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the new idea the משנה teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Birds from any nest within 50 אמות could have hopped over.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bird hops only while it can see its nest, so a nest around a corner is no concern.

steps.title: New משנה: using a pestle to cut meat on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. בית שמאי forbid taking a large pestle to cut meat on it on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: you may not take the large pestle to cut meat on it. And בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It is a dispute about using a tool on יום טוב for a job it is not usually used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pestle is usually used to crush grain, not to cut meat. בית שמאי forbid moving it for this new use, and בית הלל allow it. The question is about moving an object that is normally used for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: a large pestle used for crushing grain

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Beit Shammai say:
one may not take the large pestle
to cut meat on it,
and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים אֵין נוֹטְלִים אֶת הָעֱלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid taking the pestle to cut meat on יום טוב; בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: Putting a hide where people walk, and lifting it
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say you may not put a raw hide where people walk on it, and you may not lift it unless it has a כזית of meat on it. בית הלל permit both.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: you may not place the hide in front of those who walk on it. And you may not lift it, unless it has an olive-sized piece of meat on it. And בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל. It is about a raw animal hide on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feet walking on a raw hide help process it into leather, so בית שמאי forbid placing it there. They also treat the hide as מוקצה, so it may be lifted only together with a כזית of meat. בית הלל allow both.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נוֹתְנִין אֶת הָעוֹר לִפְנֵי הַדּוֹרְסָן.
phrases.english: one may not place the hide before those who tread on it.
And one may not lift it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ עִמּוֹ כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר,
phrases.english: unless there is an olive-bulk of meat with it,
and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים אֵין נוֹתְנִין אֶת הָעוֹר לִפְנֵי הַדּוֹרְסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second dispute in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid placing a hide to be walked on and lifting it without a כזית of meat; בית הלל permit both.

steps.title: Both sides agree: after the meat is cut, the pestle may not be moved
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that once the meat has been cut on the pestle, it may not be moved anymore.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: A ברייתא taught: Both sides agree that if a person already cut meat on the pestle, it is forbidden to move it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by quoting a ברייתא that sets a limit on בית הלל's leniency. Once the meat is cut, even בית הלל forbid moving the pestle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עלי is mainly a tool for grinding, which is forbidden on יום טוב, so it is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. בית הלל allowed handling it only because the person needed it to cut meat. Once that need is over, there is no longer any reason to permit moving it.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree (both sides of the dispute)
To move it (the issue of מוקצה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that permission to handle a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור depends on actually needing it, and the permission ends when the need ends.

phrases.english: Gemara: It was taught (in a baraita):
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא on the משנה

phrases.english: And they agree that if he cut meat on it
phrases.notes: "They" means בית שמאי and בית הלל

phrases.english: that it is forbidden to move it.
phrases.notes: The pestle goes back to being treated as מוקצה

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאִם קִצֵּב עָלָיו בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that sets the limits of the משנה's dispute about the pestle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to בית הלל, once the meat has been cut, the pestle may not be moved.

steps.title: אביי: the dispute is only about the pestle, not the bone anvil
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the argument is only about the עלי. A bone-breaking anvil is permitted according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The argument is about a pestle. But with a wooden block for breaking bones, everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets the boundaries of the dispute in the משנה. It applies only to the pestle, and not to a bone-breaking anvil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עלי's main job (grinding) is forbidden on יום טוב, so בית שמאי object to using it. A תברא גרמי's main job is breaking bones for food, which is a permitted use. So even בית שמאי agree it may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: A large pestle, mainly used for grinding grain
A wooden block or anvil for breaking bones

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The dispute is about a pestle,
but with a block for breaking bones,
everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בֶּעֱלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues clarifying the משנה, this time by limiting how far the dispute reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל is limited to the עלי. A תברא גרמי is permitted by everyone.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious? The משנה only mentions a pestle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי needs to say this. The משנה only mentions a pestle, so obviously the dispute is about a pestle.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! We learned "a pestle" in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי, saying his statement teaches nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only the עלי. So why would anyone think the bone anvil is also in dispute? אביי seems to be saying something we already know.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (the statement seems unnecessary)

phrases.english: That is obvious; we learned "a pestle"!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, עֱלִי תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether אביי's statement in Step 16 is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's statement limiting the dispute to the עלי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה itself names only the עלי, so saying the dispute does not cover a bone anvil adds nothing.

steps.title: Why אביי's statement is needed: the pestle might have been chosen just to show how far בית הלל go
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the bone anvil is also in dispute. On that reading, the משנה chose the pestle only to show that בית הלל permit even a tool made for a forbidden use. אביי teaches that this is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: The same is true even for a bone-breaking block (it is also in dispute). And the reason the משנה says "pestle" is to show you how strong בית הלל's position is: they permit even an item whose main use is forbidden. So אביי teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a mistaken way to read the משנה. אביי's statement rules out that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה often picks the most extreme case to show how far a position reaches (כחן דבית הלל). So we might think the עלי was mentioned only as the extreme case, and that בית שמאי forbid even the bone anvil. אביי teaches that בית שמאי have no complaint about a tool made for a permitted use.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken first assumption)
To show you how far their position reaches
An item whose main use is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The "מהו דתימא" part is NOT the הלכה. It is the mistaken idea that אביי is coming to correct. The real lesson is that the bone anvil is not in dispute at all.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ תָּבְרָא גַּרְמֵי נָמֵי.
phrases.english: The same applies even to a bone-breaking block as well (it is also in dispute).
phrases.notes: This is what the גמרא assumes at first, but it turns out to be a mistake.

phrases.english: And the fact that it teaches "a pestle"
is to show you how far בית הלל go,

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲפִילּוּ דָּבָר שֶׁמְּלַאכְתּוֹ לֶאֱסוֹר נָמֵי שָׁרוּ —
phrases.english: that they permit even an item whose main use is forbidden;
so he teaches us (that this is not so).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ תָּבְרָא גַּרְמֵי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reasonable mistaken reading (הוה אמינא) that makes the statement necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עלי was mentioned only to show the full reach of בית הלל, and בית שמאי forbid even a bone anvil.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is truly limited to the עלי. A bone anvil, made for a permitted use, is allowed by all.

steps.title: Second version: even a brand-new bone anvil is permitted
steps.stepSummary: In another version, אביי's point is that even a new bone-breaking anvil is permitted. We do not worry that its owner might change his mind and not use it for bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: אביי said: The point was needed only to teach that even a NEW bone-breaking block is permitted. You might have said: He may change his mind and not break bones on it. So אביי teaches us that it is still permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version (איכא דאמרי) of what אביי taught. In this version, his new point is about a new anvil, so the פשיטא question never comes up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new anvil has never been used yet. We might think its owner could decide to save it for some other use, so it does not yet count as a bone-breaking tool. אביי teaches that it is already treated as a permitted-use tool, and everyone allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for (the real new point)

steps.whatToRemember: The bone-breaking anvil is permitted by everyone, because its job is a permitted one. According to the second version, this applies even to a brand-new anvil. The dispute is only about the עלי, a tool made for a forbidden use. Even בית הלל forbid moving it once the meat has been cut.

phrases.english: Some say: Abaye said:
It was needed only for
even a new bone-breaking block,
you might have said:
He may change his mind and not break bones on it;
so he teaches us (that it is permitted).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ תָּבְרָא גַּרְמֵי חַדְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of אביי's teaching, with its own new point, so the פשיטא challenge does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a new, unused bone-breaking anvil is permitted. We do not worry that its owner will change his mind about how to use it.

steps.title: Don't בית שמאי worry that a person might change his mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the idea that בית שמאי are not worried about reconsidering. It brings a ברייתא where בית שמאי forbid moving things in case the person changes his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are בית שמאי really not worried that a person might change his mind? But a ברייתא teaches: בית שמאי say you may not bring a butcher and knife to an animal, or an animal to a butcher and knife. בית הלל say you may bring one to the other. Also, בית שמאי say you may not bring spices and a pestle to a mortar, or a mortar to spices and a pestle. בית הלל say you may bring one to the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last step. It brings a ברייתא showing that בית שמאי do worry that a person might change his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version of אביי's teaching (Step 19), even a new bone anvil is permitted, because we do not worry the owner will change his mind. But in this ברייתא, בית שמאי forbid moving a knife or a mortar for exactly that reason. If he changes his mind, he moved the item for nothing on יום טוב. So it seems בית שמאי should forbid the anvil too.

keyTerms.meaning: Pestle, the stick used for crushing
Mortar, the bowl that things are crushed in

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מָדוֹךְ and מְדוֹכָה. The מָדוֹךְ is the pestle that does the crushing. The מְדוֹכָה is the mortar, the bowl underneath.

phrases.english: And are Beit Shammai not concerned that he might change his mind?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹלִיכִין טַבָּח וְסַכִּין אֵצֶל בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: One may not bring a butcher and a knife to an animal,
nor an animal to a butcher and a knife.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מוֹלִיכִין זֶה אֵצֶל זֶה.
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: One may bring one to the other.
phrases.notes: בית הלל do not worry that he will change his mind.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹלִיכִין תַּבְלִין וּמָדוֹךְ אֵצֶל מְדוֹכָה,
phrases.english: One may not bring spices and a pestle to a mortar,
nor a mortar to spices and a pestle.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מוֹלִיכִין זֶה אֵצֶל זֶה!
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: One may bring one to the other!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי לָא חָיְישִׁי לְאִמְּלוֹכֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the second version of אביי (Step 19) as it applies to בית שמאי
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that even בית שמאי permit a new bone anvil without worrying the owner will change his mind
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows בית שמאי forbid moving a knife or a mortar because the person might change his mind. So they should worry about the anvil too.

steps.title: Changing your mind is realistic there, but not with breaking bones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. With an animal or a pot, a person might really change his mind. But once an animal is slaughtered, its bones must be broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? With an animal, he might change his mind and say: 'Let me leave this thin animal and bring a fatter one.' With a pot, he might also change his mind and say: 'Let me leave this pot that needs spices and bring a different one that does not.' But here, what can you say? That he will change his mind and not break the bones? Once he slaughtered the animal, it stands ready to have its bones broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that the cases in the ברייתא are different from the bone anvil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי only worry about changing one's mind when there is a real reason he might. A thin animal can be swapped for a fat one, and a pot that needs spices can be swapped for one that does not. But meat that is already slaughtered must be prepared, and its bones must be broken. So there is no realistic chance he will not use the anvil.

keyTerms.meaning: How can these be compared? (the cases are not alike)
It stands ready to be broken

steps.whatToRemember: Even בית שמאי only worry about changing one's mind when there is a real alternative. Once an animal is slaughtered, breaking its bones is certain. So a bone anvil is permitted according to everyone.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!
It makes sense that with an animal he might come to change his mind,
since he may say: Let us leave this thin animal,
and I will bring a different animal that is fatter than it.
With a pot too, he might come to change his mind,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: נִשְׁבֹּק הַאי קְדֵרָה דְּבָעֲיָא תַּבְלִין,
phrases.english: since he may say: Let us leave this pot, which needs spices,
and I will bring a different one that does not need spices.
Here, what is there to say?
That he will change his mind and not break the bones?
Since he slaughtered it, it stands ready to be broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא by showing the cases are not alike
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the ברייתא's cases and the bone anvil
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's cases have a realistic alternative (a fatter animal, a pot without spices). Breaking the bones of a slaughtered animal has no alternative.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since בית שמאי worry that one may change his mind about the knife and the mortar, they should worry the same way about a new bone anvil.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי worry about changing one's mind only where there is a realistic alternative (a fatter animal, a pot without spices). Once an animal is slaughtered its bones must be broken, so even בית שמאי permit a new bone anvil.

steps.title: Everyone agrees one may salt meat for roasting on a hide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה about placing a hide. It brings a ברייתא: everyone agrees one may salt meat for roasting on the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: בית שמאי say you may not place the hide. A ברייתא taught: Both agree that you may salt meat for roasting on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, about the animal's hide. It adds a ברייתא that shows where בית שמאי and בית הלל agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salting a raw hide is part of tanning, so we might worry that salt falling on it looks like tanning. Even so, the ברייתא says both sides allow salting meat for roasting on top of the hide. This sets up אביי's limit in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין נוֹתְנִין אֶת הָעוֹר.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: One may not place the hide.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, opening a new topic.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
And they agree that one may salt meat for roasting on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין נוֹתְנִין אֶת הָעוֹר. תָּנָא: וְשָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section of the משנה about the hide
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל allow salting meat for roasting on a hide on יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי limits the permission to roasting, not cooking in a pot
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the permission to salt on the hide is only for meat that will be roasted. Meat for a pot may not be salted on the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They only taught this for roasting. But for a pot, it is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a limit to the ברייתא. The permission covers roasting meat only, not meat for cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat for roasting needs only a little salt, so very little falls on the hide. Meat for a pot must be salted heavily on all sides, so a lot of salt would fall on the hide, which is like tanning it. That is why it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this for (a limiting formula)

steps.whatToRemember: One may salt meat on a hide on יום טוב only for roasting, which needs little salt. Meat for a pot needs heavy salting and may not be salted on the hide.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They taught this only for roasting,
but for a pot, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְצָלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא quoted in Step 22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salting meat on a hide is permitted only for roasting, not for meat that will be cooked in a pot.

steps.title: Why did אביי need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: the ברייתא already said 'for roasting,' so his point seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! We already learned 'for roasting'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's statement from the previous step. The ברייתא itself already said the salting is 'for roasting,' so why did אביי need to tell us that pot-meat is forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's wording 'for roasting' already implies that meat for a pot is not included. So אביי's rule seems to add nothing new. The גמרא expects every אמורא's statement to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious — 'for roasting' we learned!
phrases.notes: This refers to the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 22.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא — לְצָלִי תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether אביי's statement in Step 23 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's statement that the permission applies only to meat for roasting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already says 'for roasting,' so אביי's restriction seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Even roasting meat cannot be salted like pot meat
steps.stepSummary: אביי teaches something new. Even meat for roasting may not be salted heavily, the way one salts for a pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that even for roasting, if one salts it like meat for a pot, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אביי added a new detail. Even when the meat will be roasted, you may not salt it heavily, the way you would salt meat for a pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat for a pot needs much more salt than meat for roasting. אביי's point is about how much you salt, not only what the meat is for. Only the light salting needed for roasting is allowed on the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us (the new point)
In the manner of a pot (heavy salting)

steps.whatToRemember: Salting on the hide is allowed only for roasting, and only with the light amount of salt that roasting needs.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that even for roasting,
in the manner of a pot — it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Meat for a pot gets heavier salting.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement adds a new detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any salting for roasting meat would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only light, roasting-style salting is allowed. Heavy pot-style salting is forbidden even for roasting meat.

steps.title: A ברייתא on salting and airing the fats
steps.stepSummary: The ת״ק says one may not salt the fats or turn them over on יום טוב. רבי יהושע allows spreading them on pegs in the wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not salt the fats, and one may not turn them over. In the name of רבי יהושע they said: One may spread them out in the wind on pegs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the animal's fats (חלבים). The question is whether you may keep them from spoiling on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלבים are forbidden to eat, so they are of no use on יום טוב and count as מוקצה. That is why the ת״ק forbids salting them and even touching them to turn them over. רבי יהושע is lenient and allows spreading them on pegs so the wind keeps them from spoiling.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the חלבים are not being prepared to eat, since they are forbidden. They are only being kept from rotting so they can be used later, for example as candles or for other uses.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not salt the fats
and one may not turn them over.
In the name of Rabbi Yehoshua they said:
He may spread them out in the wind on pegs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מוֹלְחִין אֶת הַחֲלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from salting meat on the hide to a related case: preserving the fats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ת״ק: one may not salt or turn over the fats. רבי יהושע: one may spread them on pegs in the wind.

steps.title: רב מתנה rules like רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה gives a ruling on the dispute in the ברייתא. He follows the lenient view of רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this version, one may spread the fats in the wind on יום טוב. This goes against the usual rule of following the majority.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבי יהושע: one may air the fats on pegs.

steps.title: Another version: רב מתנה rules against רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב מתנה rules that the הלכה does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב מתנה said: The הלכה does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב מתנה's ruling, which says the opposite. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have two opposite reports of the same ruling. Each one will need to show that it teaches something new, and the גמרא checks that next.

phrases.english: Some say: Rav Mattana said:
The halacha is not like Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of the ruling in Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha does not follow רבי יהושע. The ת״ק's restriction stands.

steps.title: Why say the halacha follows the majority?
steps.stepSummary: The first version makes sense, but the second version seems obvious, since we always follow the majority over one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for the one who says the הלכה follows רבי יהושע: that needed to be said. You might have thought that with one against many, the הלכה follows the many, so he teaches that it follows the individual. But for the one who says the הלכה does not follow him, it is obvious! With one against many, the הלכה follows the many!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the first version teaches something new. Then it challenges the second version: following the majority is the normal rule, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע is one person against the ת״ק, who stand for the many. Ruling for one person is surprising and worth saying. Ruling for the majority is the default, so that version seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (sets up a contrast)

phrases.english: It is fine according to the one who says
'the halacha is like Rabbi Yehoshua' — it was needed,
for it would enter your mind to say
'one against many — the halacha is like the many,'
so he teaches us the halacha is like the individual.
But according to the one who says 'the halacha is not' —
it is obvious: one against many — the halacha is like the many!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ — אִצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both versions of רב מתנה. The first passes; the second is challenged.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רב מתנה (Step 28)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following the majority is the default rule, so saying it seems useless.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's reasoning is strong, yet we do not follow it
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed, because רבי יהושע's reason sounds convincing: if you forbid this, people may stop slaughtering on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי יהושע's reason makes sense, because if you don't allow him, he will hold back and not slaughter. So he teaches us that we still don't follow him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Without this ruling, we might have followed רבי יהושע because his reason sounds strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's concern is that a person who cannot save the valuable fats will not slaughter at all, and that would lessen the joy of יום טוב. Because this reason is so convincing, we might have overridden the majority. רב מתנה teaches that this concern does not override the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: He will hold back and not slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of רב מתנה teach something new. The first rules for the individual against the majority. The second tells us not to follow רבי יהושע, even though his reason (people might stop slaughtering) is strong.

phrases.english: You might have said:
Rabbi Yehoshua's reasoning makes sense,
for if you do not permit him,
he will hold back and not slaughter,
so he teaches us (that we do not follow this).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: מִסְתַּבַּר טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against the second version in Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement removes a reasonable mistaken assumption (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's reason is strong enough to override the majority, so the halacha would follow him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern that people will stop slaughtering does not override the majority, so the halacha does not follow רבי יהושע.

steps.title: How is this different from placing a hide before treaders?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we reject רבי יהושע's reasoning here when the same reasoning is accepted for placing a hide before those who tread on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from placing a hide before those who tread on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version of רב מתנה, which rules against רבי יהושע. It points to another case where we do accept the worry that people will stop slaughtering on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית הלל allow putting a fresh animal hide where people will walk on it. They allow this because otherwise people might avoid slaughtering on יום טוב, and the הלכה follows בית הלל. If that worry is enough to permit the hide, it should also be enough to permit spreading the fats, as רבי יהושע says. So why does רב מתנה rule against him?

keyTerms.meaning: And how is it different? A standard way to challenge an inconsistency between two cases
Hide, the skin of a slaughtered animal
Those who tread or trample. Walking on a fresh hide helps begin the tanning process
The school of הלל, whose permissive ruling on the hide is accepted as הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא names the hide case explicitly ('עור לפני הדורסן'), but it does not state בית הלל's reason. It assumes you know that בית הלל permit the hide because of the same worry: that otherwise people will stop slaughtering on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And what is different
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pointing out that two cases seem to be treated differently, and asks why.

phrases.english: from placing a hide before those who tread on it?
phrases.notes: This refers to בית הלל's lenient ruling in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מֵעוֹר לִפְנֵי הַדּוֹרְסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 30 granted that רבי יהושע's reasoning sounds convincing. This step argues that the same reasoning is actually accepted elsewhere, so it should be accepted here too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רב מתנה's ruling, that the הלכה does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inconsistency between cases. בית הלל permit the hide out of concern that people will stop slaughtering, and the הלכה follows them. The same concern underlies רבי יהושע's leniency for the fats, so rejecting it here seems inconsistent.
